Data quality / Consistency

Source-to-dashboard reconciliation rate

A configured validation measure of eligible source records represented correctly in the destination, using agreed keys, field mappings, and tolerances. It checks whether important sales or marketing facts survived ingestion and transformation.

Explore in the metric hierarchy ↗Open calculators →
Level 4Inspect the detail

A configured validation measure of eligible source records represented correctly in the destination, using agreed keys, field mappings, and tolerances. It checks whether important sales or marketing facts survived ingestion and transformation.

%

How we use it

We can compare record IDs, amounts, counts, and totals between source systems and BI models, with an exception queue for mismatches.

Transparent calculationEligible source records passing all agreed destination-match checks ÷ all eligible source records expected in the destination × 100
source records passing match checks9,900
eligible expected source records10,000

9,900 ÷ 10,000 × 100 = 99% matched records; 100 expected records need investigation.

Illustrative calculation. Not a client result or a universal benchmark.

Break the result down

  • Source and destination pair
  • Record type and match rule
  • Load period and exception reason

Questions we investigate

  • Which expected source records fail agreed matches?
  • Do duplicates or extras exist at the destination?
  • Are match tolerance and timing rules consistent?

Actions the evidence supports

  • Investigate failed records with source owners.
  • Repair mappings and deduplication rules.
  • Review missing matches and extra records separately.

Reporting contract

Ownership & cadence

Data quality and business system leads
After material loads and at financial close where relevant.

Required data

  • Eligible expected source-record IDs
  • Destination records and agreed match-check results
  • Match tolerance, timing, and exception rules

Read the measure with context

Zero expected source records makes the rate undefined. Matching row counts alone cannot prove accurate values. Define currency, rounding, cutoffs, deletions, and aggregation rules. Report duplicate or unexpected destination records separately; this source-denominator rate alone cannot detect every excess record.
